content.thinking:
I'm checking each claim against the source material. The account-page failure duration and "some" shoppers both hold up, and so does the peak error rate. The customer loss estimate also checks out, as does the note that nobody was paged. The last line, about the administrator switching off the older fallback, is supported as the cause.

I'm checking the rest of the claims: Argus reverted the monthly-spend feature first, which didn't help, so it was restored. It then reverted the legacy checkout fallback, which was confirmed as still in place. Finally, Argus has proposed a fix as a draft pull request that hasn't been applied yet.

supported.quote: On io-shop, some shoppers' account pages failed to load for {duration}.
rows: What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load

supported.quote: At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing
rows: Requests failing at the worst minute: 33.5% {peak_error_rate}

supported.quote: Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 8,013.46 USD {customer_loss}

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: It started when an administrator switched off an older fallback for showing shoppers their account pages.
That sent those pages through newer code, which most likely breaks when it works out a shopper's average spend for the month if the shopper has bought nothing that month.
Argus first reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature, but that did not help, so Argus put it back.
Argus then reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback. That revert was confirmed and is still in place.
Argus has also proposed a fix, which is open as a draft and has not yet been applied.
rows: Argus: proposed a fix, PR #549 - opened as a draft
The fix it proposed: PR #549 ... opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
